scopes.finite_question: At the current 16f9eefa source, can the actual SYCL prefill MoE output/scratch reservations safely hold FP16 expert outputs for two consecutive 8192-row causal chunks represented as one expert-major 16384-row window? Reconstruct exact producers, consumers, routes, dimensions, alignments, allocations, and live intervals; compare the proposed window with the current per-chunk path and existing opt-in compact FP16 behavior. Determine which scratch bytes are genuinely reusable at every phase, and whether batching/reordering expert output work can occur while QSA, GDN/recurrent state, shared expert work, callbacks, checkpoints, and layer publication retain their current required order.
scopes.breadth_and_counterevidence: Build one source-backed live-range table for GU, Hh, Dm, route/index arrays, shared-expert inputs/outputs, native16 temporaries, and relevant state/publication buffers. Show exact current element and byte capacities, alignment/padding, whether each plane aliases a larger FP32 reservation, and simultaneous peak bytes. Compare (a) present 8192 chunk storage, (b) two sequential FP16 chunks, and (c) the proposed contiguous expert-major 16384 window; distinguish serialized reuse from concurrently live storage and include route multiplicity/top-k and per-expert offsets. Check the existing STRATA_PREFILL_MOE_COMPACT_FP16 guard/fallback so an existing code path is not described as new. Map the outer operator order and publication points needed to preserve QSA/GDN state and physical-context behavior. Counterevidence must include any path/mode where the slot is not available, shape/alignment/streaming or peer constraints that block aliasing, any required conversion or extra transfer, and any ordering dependency that prevents a two-chunk window. A byte-capacity match alone is not an implementation recommendation. Keep FP16 numerical error, quality acceptance, performance, and default adoption as separate unanswered gates; keep FP32 accumulation, router decisions and recurrent state wherever current source requires them. Do not infer MoE service or speed from the nonexclusive unitrace totals.

scopes.finite_question: For single-GPU equijoins, compare direct GPU hash build/probe, radix-partitioned hash join, and sort-merge as a counterpoint. How do build/probe size ratio, duplicate fanout, key-frequency and partition skew, key/payload width, table load factor, available device memory, and output materialization change the time/space crossover or create failure modes?
scopes.breadth_and_counterevidence: Use original GPU join papers and primary accelerator/database sources. Compare algorithms by build, partition, probe/merge, overflow/spill, and output phases in one table; record GPU generation, relation sizes, key/payload types, skew distribution, memory residency, and timing boundary. Include at least one case where partitioning or sort-merge wins and one where its extra passes or materialization lose; explain why direct hash-table results do not automatically predict end-to-end join time. Preserve many-to-many duplicate semantics and distinguish skew in key frequency from skew in partition occupancy. Keep source-specific measurements separate and do not compare cross-paper speedups as a controlled ranking.
scopes.novelty_guard: R867 covered operator fusion/materialization boundaries and expressly left hash-join algorithm design outside its survey. This scope is only the single-GPU equijoin algorithm and its build/probe/capacity crossover. Exclude query fusion, query planning, group-by, theta joins, general-purpose hash-table surveys beyond supporting a join mechanism, CPU/GPU co-processing, multi-GPU execution, product changes, and Strata/Arc performance claims. Do not read held R867-R869 knowledge bodies.

scopes.finite_question: For dense fully connected/MLP layers in non-LLM inference ASICs, compare weight-stationary, output-stationary, row-stationary, and flexible spatial dataflows. How do batch size and M/K/N shape, local buffer capacity, PE-array dimensions, partial-sum movement, and interconnect flexibility alter operand reuse, off-chip traffic, utilization, energy, and latency? Identify workload regimes where a fixed dataflow wins and where a flexible mapping or a different stationary choice recovers otherwise idle compute or excess movement.
scopes.breadth_and_counterevidence: Use a small number of original ASIC architecture papers and primary model/documentation sources. Compare dataflows under clearly stated equal-area or equal-resource assumptions where sources provide them, and keep measured silicon results distinct from analytical models and simulated mapping exploration. Include one result favoring stationary reuse and at least two counterexamples involving narrow or small-batch layers, array tails/low utilization, partial-sum traffic, SRAM capacity, or interconnect cost. State matrix shapes, batch, bit widths, array dimensions, buffer assumptions, and timing/energy boundary for each quantitative claim. The output should be a mechanism comparison, not a recommendation for a specific product or a claim about desktop GPU performance.
scopes.novelty_guard: Keep the scope at architecture-level spatial-array dataflow for non-LLM fully connected/MLP inference. R855 is GPU convolution mapping; R839 is local-memory bank mapping; prior GEMM tile/operand-layout studies concern GPU kernel geometry.
